source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for Scabies
source.publisher: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

sections.label: Signs of Severe or Complicated Scabies: See a Doctor
items: Crusted (Norwegian) scabies: thick, yellow-brown crusts on the skin, particularly on the hands and feet, this is a severe form seen in people with weak immunity and is highly contagious
Signs of secondary bacterial infection: skin that is red, swollen, warm, and has pus or a foul smell
Scabies in someone who is immunocompromised (on steroids, with HIV, or on chemotherapy), this can become very severe quickly
Widespread scabies outbreak in a school, orphanage, or shared-living setting

sections.label: Self-Care and Household Measures
items: All family members and close physical contacts must be treated at the same time, even if they have no symptoms, treating only the affected person will lead to re-infestation
Wash all clothes, towels, and bedlinen used in the past three days in hot water and dry them in the sun
Items that cannot be washed (shoes, bags) can be sealed in a plastic bag for at least 3 days, the mite cannot survive without human contact
Do not share clothing, towels, or bedding with others during the infestation
Maintain good general hygiene throughout treatment
Important: itching can continue for several weeks after successful treatment, this is normal and does not mean the treatment has failed
Do not repeat the treatment application just because itching continues, continue antihistamines for relief instead
If new lesions appear or itching continues for more than 3 to 4 weeks after treatment, re-infestation is likely, this usually means a close contact was not treated

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Intense itching that is worse at night, especially in the fingers, wrists, belly button area, breasts, buttocks, or genitals
Other family members developing the same symptoms
Small, red, itchy bumps or burrow marks between the fingers or on the wrists
Itching and rash with no obvious cause in a child
Persistent itching and new lesions after completing a course of treatment
Any sign of secondary skin infection (pus, crusting, fever)

sections.label: Refer to Higher Centre
items: Crusted (Norwegian) scabies, requires specialised treatment and isolation precautions
Scabies in an immunocompromised person
Secondary bacterial infection that is spreading or not responding to treatment
Persistent, treatment-resistant nodular lesions over the genitals

review.notes: All topical and oral drug names, application instructions, and dosing excluded. Core household and contact-tracing measures retained as these are essential for treatment success and do not involve drug advice.
